name: Free Source Check Studio Lesson PowerPoint Template
description: An editable source evaluation lesson for teaching learners to separate a claim from its evidence, question a source, and explain a careful conclusion.
longDescription: This original eight-slide source evaluation lesson gives teachers a complete classroom sequence: a question, learning goal, sample claim, source check, evidence comparison, guided practice, reflection, and next action. A claim-ledger visual system uses offset evidence strips, large verdict stamps, and a warm cream, aubergine, coral, and teal palette. Every element is editable PowerPoint text or a native shape. All sample numbers are illustrative placeholders and should be replaced with verified classroom material.
cover: A practical lesson for checking a claim before sharing it.

story.title: What would make this claim trustworthy?
story.body: Start with a fictional claim and invite learners to name what they need to know.
points: What is the claim asking us to believe?

story.title: Name the checks before the search
story.body: Learners practice tracing an author, date, and supporting evidence.
points: Look for a source that can be examined

story.title: Separate the statement from its support
story.body: Use a teacher-made example to show the difference between confidence and proof.

story.title: Trace the path back to an origin
story.body: Check who published the material and whether the cited evidence is accessible.

story.title: One signal is not the whole picture
story.body: Compare independent evidence and record where sources agree or differ.

story.title: Build a careful evidence note
story.body: Pairs make a provisional judgment and explain which check changed their view.
points: Say what would change the conclusion

story.title: Share a conclusion with its limits
story.body: Close by naming the best-supported statement and one open question.
points: State only what the evidence supports
